archival_observation: A document preserved in the Arthur O. Lovejoy Papers can be addressed to someone other than Lovejoy.
what_is_secure: repository custody/fonds attribution plus cited sender-recipient-date-box
what_is_not_secure: how the document entered Lovejoy's custody; whether it is an original, copy, enclosure, forwarded letter, committee file copy, or later insertion
data_model_consequence: model archival_custody separately from sender and recipient; never infer recipient from fonds creator
example: Tyler to Stone, 31 Jan 1919, Lovejoy Papers Box83
verification_path: inspect physical item for salutation/address, copy marks, docket, enclosure and provenance evidence

archival_observation: Lovejoy-authored outgoing correspondence can also survive in Lovejoy's own papers.
what_is_secure: Lovejoy authorship/direction as cited plus Lovejoy-fonds custody
what_is_not_secure: whether surviving manifestation is draft, carbon, letterpress copy, retained copy, returned original, or transcription
data_model_consequence: add manifestation_form with UNKNOWN as a valid value; sender=Lovejoy plus custody=Lovejoy does not define physical form
example: Lovejoy to Tyler, 18 Feb 1919, Lovejoy Papers Box83
verification_path: inspect paper/typewriting/handwriting/copy marks and compare recipient-side archive if found

archival_observation: A box can mix bilateral correspondence with institutional traffic among third parties.
what_is_secure: multiple exact Tiede citations place both categories in Boxes24 and83
what_is_not_secure: whether repository arrangement treats these documents as one correspondence file, a subject/case file, enclosures, or redistributed items
data_model_consequence: mechanical harvest must enumerate documents by sender-recipient and documentary role, not only by named correspondent component
example: Box24: Young to Tyler; Hobbs/Ely to Young. Box83: Tyler to Lillie/Stone/Kellogg alongside Tyler-Lovejoy traffic.
verification_path: recover current folder structure and inspect adjacency/order before reconstructing original filing logic

archival_observation: A correspondent index is a useful topology generator but is not an inventory of all documentary actors represented in a personal fonds.
what_is_secure: named MS-0038 correspondent components remain valid exact locators
what_is_not_secure: absence of a person's named correspondent component does not imply absence of documents by/to that person elsewhere in case/organizational files
data_model_consequence: supplement correspondent topology with document-ecology layer and third-party-document register
example: Tyler to Stone in Box83 exists by exact scholarly citation even though current public MS-0038 correspondent harvest has not surfaced a Tyler component
verification_path: top-container -> folder -> item enumeration plus citation-driven date search

archival_observation: Repository custody and historical document-event identity are separate entities.
what_is_not_secure: whether a document is the same manifestation/event as a copy in another repository
data_model_consequence: assign shared document_event_id only after date/direction/content/form collation
example: 31 Jan Tyler to Stone in Lovejoy B83 versus Stone personal papers B37 as a reciprocal search path
verification_path: search Stone B37 for corresponding incoming item and compare text/material evidence
